To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Broucke family of periodic orbits in the planar circular restricted three-body problem, when restricted to the energy E=-0,5 plane, is topologically dense and that the angular momentum L of these solutions is a linear function of the period of the orbit T and the topological exponent of the satellite k.
the angular momentum and topological dependence of Kepler's third law are the same for both the Broucke and Broucke-Hénon families of periodic orbits.

the angular momentum L and the period T of periodic orbits in the Brouke-Hadjidemetrious-Hénon family of solutions of the three-body problem are related through a Kepler's third law-like relation, that the topological satellites of periodic orbits in this family obey the same relation, and that the standard deviation of the topological satellites from the progenitor data for nonsatellite periodic orbits is small, σ=0.12.

the topological dependence of Kepler's third law for periodic orbits in the three-body problem.
the angular momentum and topological dependence of Kepler's Third law for the Broucke- Hadjidemetriou-Hénons periodic orbits.
the stability and topological dependence of the angular momentum of the Broucke- Hadjidemetriou-Hénons periodic orbits.

Kepler's third law is valid for all orbits in this family of periodic orbits.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Kepler's third law is a topological property.
the angular momentum and period of the Broucke family of periodic orbits depend only on the topological exponent, and not on any of the other orbital parameters.

the topological dependence of Kepler's third law in the Brouke-Hadjidemetrious-Hénon family of periodic three-body orbits is virtually indiscermible from the topological independence of Kepler's third in Newtonian three-body dynamics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the topological dependence of L(T) is negligible, at least for the Broucke- Hadjidemetrióu-Hénon family.
Kepler's third law is topologically dependent, in the sense that the L(T) curves for nonsatellites and satellites of the same topological class are indiscernible.
Kepler's third law is not a fundamental law of celestial mechanics but is rather a topological artifact of the three-body problem.
